title: From Hourly to Annual: Understanding Your Pay, Tax, and the Minimum Wage 2026
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual pay using the 38-hour week. Includes tax, Medicare levy, superannuation, and the minimum wage 2026 figures.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52, and the 2026 National Minimum Wage of $26.44/hour gives about $52,253 before tax.

faqs.q: How is annual pay calculated from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the formula is hourly rate × 38 × 52. This assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. The result is your gross annual salary before tax and other deductions.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum pay for employees not covered by an award or agreement. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour (or $1004.90 per week for 38 hours). Award rates are industry- or occupation-specific minimums set by the Fair Work Commission and are often higher. Your actual pay may be above the minimum if your award or agreement specifies a higher rate.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my pay and super?
faqs.a: Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. For example, the minimum wage 2026 casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). Superannuation is calculated on your ordinary earnings, which includes the casual loading. So your super guarantee contribution (12% in 2026–27) is based on the loaded rate, not the base rate.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

If you earn an hourly wage or have a salary offer, you can estimate your annual gross pay using a simple formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. This calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For most full-time employees, the standard week is 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. When you use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool, we assume 38 hours unless you tell us otherwise.

### The Minimum Wage 2026

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage set by the Fair Work Commission is **$26.44 per hour** (or $1004.90 per week for 38 hours). This is the legal floor for employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. If you are a casual worker, you also receive a 25% loading, making the minimum wage 2026 casual rate **$33.05 per hour**. Remember, this is a minimum – many awards and enterprise agreements pay higher rates. For a detailed breakdown, see our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page.

## Tax and the Medicare Levy

Once you have your annual gross figure, the next step is understanding how much tax and the Medicare levy you will pay. The Australian Taxation Office uses a progressive tax scale for residents in 2026–27:

- **Nil** on income up to $18,200
- **15%** on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- **30%** on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- **37%** on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- **45%** on income above $190,000

In addition, most residents pay the **Medicare levy** of 2% of taxable income. For 2026–27, the single reduction thresholds are not yet confirmed, so we use the 2025–26 figures (which are lower). This means our estimate may slightly overstate your levy if you qualify for a reduction. The levy applies to all taxable income above the tax-free threshold.

### Example: Minimum Wage 2026 Annual Pay

Take the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week. Annual gross = $26.44 × 38 × 52 = **$52,253.44** (rounded). Using the 2026–27 tax scale and 2% Medicare levy:

- Tax-free portion: $18,200
- Tax on next $26,800 (up to $45,000): 15% = $4,020
- Tax on remaining $7,053.44 (over $45,000): 30% = $2,116.03
- Total tax: $6,136.03
- Medicare levy (2% of $52,253.44): $1,045.07
- Total deductions: $7,181.10
- **Estimated annual take-home pay: $45,072.34**

This is an estimate only. Your actual tax may differ if you have HELP debt, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. For a more personalised estimate, use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator.

## Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation guarantee contributions are paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the rate is **12%** of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For the minimum wage example above, your employer would contribute an extra $6,270.41 per year (12% of $52,253.44). This is not deducted from your pay – it is an additional benefit. If you earn above the maximum base, super only applies up to that limit. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. For a 38-hour week at $26.44 per hour, weekly pay is $1,004.90, so fortnightly is **$2,009.80** before tax. After tax and Medicare, your fortnightly take-home would be roughly $1,733.55 (using the annual estimate divided by 26). This can help you budget for bills and savings.

## Casual Loading and Award Rates

If you are a casual employee, your hourly rate includes a 25% loading to compensate for not receiving paid leave (annual leave, sick leave). The loading is applied to the base rate. For the minimum wage 2026, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour. When using our calculator, you can tick a checkbox to add 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate – **do not** enter a rate that already includes loading. The loading affects your annual gross and, consequently, your tax and super. For more details, see [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading).

Award rates are set by the Fair Work Commission for specific industries and occupations. They are often higher than the National Minimum Wage. For example, a retail employee may have a higher minimum hourly rate under the Retail Award. Always check your award or agreement to ensure you are being paid correctly. Our [pay guides](/blog) can help you find the right rate.

## Important Considerations

This conversion assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It also assumes no salary sacrifice arrangements. Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed in this estimate. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For a quick calculation, use our [timesheet](/). For detailed reference tables, visit [reference tables](/data). Always consult a tax professional for personal advice.
